title: Turning Artwork into Interactive Game Elements
author: Chemical-Reindeer-56
selftext:
Hey reddit aigamedev! I’m the developer of **Simu Engine**, and I’d love feedback from people working with AI-generated game UI artwork.

Generating a screen is one step. Making its buttons, text, inputs, and navigation actually work is another. Usually, developers have to rebuild the flow from your AI-gen concept art in a game engine to make it game elements. However, rebuilding a game UI element from concept art is a pain in the ass, and not mention that u lose some details you really really like from the concept art in the rebuilding process.

Simu Engine is my attempt to make that part easier by turning concept arts directly into game elements, bypassing the rebuilding steps.

It has two parts:

* **Simu Editor:** import PNG/JPEG artwork, define interactive regions, and configure controls and editable text.
* **Simu Builder:** connect those screens into a project, preview the flow, and export it.
* **CLI tools:** access the authoring workflow through scripts or coding agents. (THIS IS THE MAIN WORKFLOW).

You establish your Game Rules by telling your agent who has CLI connects to the tool. Everything can be done from one agent console you're working with.

  
This is an early developer preview that runs locally in your browser. It requires **Python 3.12+**, with internet needed for the initial dependency installation. I’ve tested the package on macOS; Windows/Linux launchers are included but remain unverified. Automatic text detection currently requires macOS, with manual authoring available otherwise.

  
If you try it, a useful first experiment would be to generate two screens you want to connect together using any LLM u like, then ask your main agent to use CLI to Simu Edit any details you want with the image, then connect them together using CLI for Simu Builder.

  
I’m especially interested in:

* Where setup or the workflow gets confusing.
* What prevents you from using your own artwork.
* Whether this saves time compared with your current approach.

Download link is: [https://github.com/SebastianHoang/simu-engine-downloads.git](https://github.com/SebastianHoang/simu-engine-downloads.git)

  
If you are interested, I'm looking for some handsome co-engineer fellows to help me build this Engine. We can use this engine for many game purposes: Visual novels, Dating Simulator, Turn-based game, etc.

I'm also researching and developing integrating motions and animations into the Engine making as well.

I would really value some feedbacks, please give it a try ! Thanks for reading !
